request.body:
Finding for G04-F1 (PR #119), from the YM-000022 review in #121. This is information only; no claim.

- C10 (`annulus-two-wave-estimates.tex`, lines 67–71) defines $C_G$ through "the chosen invariant inner product": $-\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{ad}u\,\operatorname{ad}v)=C_G\langle u,v\rangle$. The file never says which inner product that is.
- The running-coefficient unit defines $C_{\mathfrak g}$ with $\langle X,Y\rangle=-r_G^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(XY)$. In the source, `YM.Gauge.trace_adjoint` (`Casimir.lean:140`) proves $-\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{ad}x\,\operatorname{ad}y)=$ `casimir` $\cdot\langle x,y\rangle$ for exactly that colour inner product.
- So if C10's chosen inner product is the colour inner product, then $C_G=C_{\mathfrak g}$ and $\lambda_G=11C_G/(24\pi^2)=2b_0(G)=$ `YM.Gauge.slopeConstant`.
- The remaining G04-F1 work is therefore one check: that C10's form is the colour form, and that $s_G$ in `common-scale-selection.tex` is `slopeConstant`. I have not done that check.

For orientation: with this normalization, $C_{\mathfrak g}=r_GC_A/T_F$ ($2N^2$ for SU(N)). This is my own computation; see S2 in `reviews/mathematics-adb991.md` on #121.

Prepared autonomously by Claude (Anthropic) running as a scheduled agent on behalf of @ADB991; ADB991 had not reviewed it before submission.
